 Georgia breaks record for early voting in a midterm election
 Voting 
 Patrick Saunders 
 | WABE 
 October 29th, 2026
 Updated October 29, 2026,
 5:08 PM EDT 
 Campaign signs were posted outside the early voting location at Beulah Heights University in Southeast Atlanta on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. (Jess Mador/WABE)
 Georgia voters broke the state’s record for early in-person voting in a midterm election on Thursday, crossing the 2.3 million mark set four years ago. 
 The milestone came as early voting nears its end on Friday. 
 The state is also well on its way to breaking the record for overall early voting in a Georgia midterm election — that’s in-person plus absentee voting. That record of 2.5 million votes was set in 2022 .
 Over 30% of Georgia’s 7.5 million active voters have turned out so far as of Thursday afternoon. White voters account for about half of the turnout, followed by Black voters at about 30%, Hispanic voters at about 3%, and Asian voters at about 2%.
 There is a marked difference in early voting turnout by gender, with women accounting for 56% of the vote compared to men at 44%. 
 Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger celebrated the state’s record-breaking pace on Thursday.
 “Georgians continue to head to the polls in record numbers because they trust the system,” he said in a press release. “This record-breaking in-person early voting turnout wouldn’t be possible without our county elections officials who work every day to ensure our elections are free, fair, and fast.”
 Georgia mail voting plummeted this year 
 While the state is setting records for early in-person voting, the number of people voting by mail this year has plunged. 
 Nearly 250,000 people voted by mail in the 2022 midterm election. As of Thursday afternoon, only about 110,000 people have voted by mail. 
 2026 Georgia Midterm Elections 
 Stay in the know with WABE’s 2026 Georgia Midterm Election page, where you can find the latest election news, important dates, voting locations, candidate info, results and more.
 Raffensperger reminded voters that all absentee ballots must be received by their county’s election office by 7 p.m. on Election Day on Tuesday. Ballots postmarked by then but not received will not count.
 “With Election Day fast approaching, be mindful that ballots must be returned to your county elections office by the time polls close,” Raffensperger said Thursday. “Per Georgia law, you may hand-deliver your completed ballot to your county elections office by 7 p.m. on Election Day. Official drop boxes are only available during designated early-voting hours.”
 Georgia voters who requested an absentee ballot but haven’t received it can still vote in person on Tuesday. 
 “Local election officials can help you cancel your absentee ballot and cast your vote,” Raffenperger said. 
 Trump, Obama, Harris visit Georgia in election’s final days
 The state is seeing a slew of notable visitors in the final days of early voting. President Donald Trump held a campaign rally in Perry on Saturday — his second visit to Georgia this month. 
 Former President Barack Obama appeared at a rally in Morrow on Wednesday with former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms, Sen. Jon Ossoff and several other Democratic candidates. Bottoms is facing billionaire healthcare executive Rick Jackson in the governor’s race, while Ossoff is facing U.S. Rep. Mike Collins in his reelection bid. 
 “Everywhere you go, it feels like change is in the air,” Obama said at the rally.
 Former Vice President Kamala Harris will be in Georgia on Thursday and Friday to get out the Democratic vote.
 Some Georgia Republicans are looking to turn away from the national political environment in the election’s final days.
 “Look, it’s a tough environment,” Gov. Brian Kemp said at a Tuesday rally for Jackson. “We might as well own that. We knew that, you know, two years ago. But we got a great record and a great story to tell in our state. We got to keep telling it. We can’t let the Democrats nationalize this election.”
 Bottoms was asked about nationalizing her race while speaking to reporters in Southwest Atlanta on Tuesday.
 “The nation’s paying attention,” she said. “This race is about Georgia, but Georgia is an important part of what happens across this country.”
 Georgia voters choosing numerous down-ballot candidates
 There are consequential races up and down the ballot this year, including for U.S. Senate, governor and other statewide offices, all 14 U.S. House seats, every seat in the state legislature, and many local seats.
 Most of the Georgia candidates for federal and statewide office met in a series of debates hosted by the Atlanta Press Club earlier this month. 
 Find your nearest Georgia early voting location , and dive deeper into Georgia’s early voting turnout numbers with the Secretary of State’s election data hub .
 What’s on your ballot depends on where you live. To see which offices are up for a vote in your area, visit the Georgia Secretary of State’s My Voter Page to view your sample ballot.
 Early voting for Georgia’s midterm election runs through Friday. Election Day is Nov. 3.
 WABE’s Rahul Bali contributed to this report.
